beats.subline: Thursday, August 20, 2026 close — stocks fell as Treasury-yield relief faded, Walmart tumbled on weak guidance, and Iran tensions pushed oil higher.
beats.body: The Dow led losses as Walmart shares sank roughly 9% on disappointing guidance, while the 30-year Treasury yield resumed climbing despite the Treasury's debt-buyback intervention earlier in the week, and Brent crude rose after Trump threatened 'economic warfare' against Iran.

beats.headline: North Korea fires over 10 ballistic missiles as Trump-ordered US drills wind down
beats.body: North Korea launched more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast Thursday, prompting an emergency security meeting in Seoul, days after President Trump ordered a substantial reduction in the annual US-South Korea Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise in a bid to court Kim Jong Un; Trump has said he plans to visit Kim later this year.

beats.headline: Taiwan tracks 14 Chinese ships, 7 PLA aircraft in latest 24-hour window
beats.body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense said it tracked seven PLA aircraft, eight PLA Navy vessels and six other official ships in the 24 hours to 6 a.m. Thursday, with five of the seven aircraft sorties entering Taiwan's northern, southwestern and eastern air defense identification zone; the ministry has now logged Chinese military aircraft 159 times and ships 247 times so far this month.

beats.headline: USS George Washington arrives in Middle East, leaving no US carrier in the Western Pacific
beats.body: The carrier USS George Washington reached the CENTCOM region Wednesday to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose crew has endured a record-length deployment marked by reports of poor morale and multiple overboard incidents; the handoff leaves the US without a forward-deployed aircraft carrier west of San Diego, underscoring the strain the Iran war has placed on the carrier fleet.

beats.headline: General Atomics unveils Wildfire drone as its pitch to succeed the MQ-9 Reaper
beats.body: General Atomics entered its new Wildfire unmanned aircraft into the Pentagon's competition for a next-generation medium-altitude, long-endurance ISR and strike drone, targeting a 10,000-nautical-mile ferry range, the ability to carry four Long Range Anti-Ship Missiles and control of up to 100 aircraft in semi-autonomous swarms; the push for a cheaper Reaper successor follows the loss of roughly a quarter of the US MQ-9 fleet during the Iran war.

beats.headline: Anthropic to let enterprise customers store Claude data on their own cloud
beats.body: Anthropic plans to soften a June policy requiring 30 days of logged traffic on its most powerful models for cyberattack monitoring, saying business customers can now keep that required 30-day data on their own cloud infrastructure instead of Anthropic's; the shift follows months of pushback from more than 100 enterprise customers, including Salesforce, and comes as rival OpenAI touts a zero-retention safety system.

beats.headline: Bears CB Kyler Gordon's roster spot in doubt as calf injury lingers
beats.body: Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs reported that Gordon, still on the physically-unable-to-perform list with a calf injury that has kept him off the practice field all camp, has fading odds of making the initial 53-man roster before the Aug. 30 cutdown, with a season-opening stint on injured reserve now the more likely path.

beats.headline: Byron heads to New Hampshire for a low-pressure tune-up before the playoffs
beats.body: William Byron and the No. 24 Hendrick Motorsports team head into this weekend's Dollar Tree 301 at New Hampshire Motor Speedway, set for Sunday, treating it as a low-key opportunity to build consistency before the NASCAR Cup Series playoffs begin next month; Byron won a Truck Series race at the track in 2016 but has yet to win there in Cup competition.

beats.body: No new PCA-specific development from a reputable outlet surfaced within the 72-hour window beyond the June General Assembly and stated clerk transition already reported in prior briefs.
